svg.text: Exhaustive row algorithm — rows bottom-up, pivot applied to every column to its right

text.tspan: Same matrix: R ← D, V ← I. Rows are now processed from the bottom up. For row i, lft(i) is the earliest column whose
lowest non-zero entry lies in row i (green column); it is applied to the orange columns, eliminating the ringed entries.
Row 8: columns with lowest entry here: 3, 8. lft(8) = 3 (green) is the pivot, (8, 3).
Apply it to column 8 (orange): every column to the right with an entry in row 8.
Column 8 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 8 = {1, 4, 5, 6}.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 7: columns with lowest entry here: 6, 7. lft(7) = 6 (green) is the pivot, (7, 6).
Apply it to column 7 (orange): every column to the right with an entry in row 7.
Column 7 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 7 = {1, 5}.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 6: columns with lowest entry here: 8. lft(6) = 8 (green) is the pivot, (6, 8).
Row 6 is already zero to the right of the pivot: nothing to apply.
Row 5: columns with lowest entry here: 1, 7. lft(5) = 1 (green) is the pivot, (5, 1).
Apply it to columns 3, 6, 7, 8 (orange): every column to the right with an entry in row 5.
Columns 3, 6, 7, 8 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 3 = {2, 4, 6, 8} column 6 = {1, 4, 7} column 7 = {2, 4} column 8 = {2, 6}.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 4: columns with lowest entry here: 4, 5, 7. lft(4) = 4 (green) is the pivot, (4, 4).
Apply it to columns 5, 6, 7 (orange): every column to the right with an entry in row 4.
Columns 5, 6, 7 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 5 = {1, 2, 3} column 6 = {1, 2, 3, 7} column 7 = {3}.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 3: columns with lowest entry here: 5, 7. lft(3) = 5 (green) is the pivot, (3, 5).
Apply it to columns 6, 7 (orange): every column to the right with an entry in row 3.
Columns 6, 7 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 6 = {7} column 7 = {1, 2}.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 2: columns with lowest entry here: 2, 7. lft(2) = 2 (green) is the pivot, (2, 2).
Apply it to columns 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 (orange): every column to the right with an entry in row 2.
Columns 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 updated (dark gray = changed entries): column 3 = {1, 4, 6, 8} column 4 = {1, 3, 4} column 5 = {3} column 7 = 0 column 8 = {1, 6}.
The same column additions were applied to V.
Row 1: no column has its lowest non-zero entry in this row (columns 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 have entries here, but their pivots lie further down).
lft(1) is undefined: row 1 holds no pivot.
Identical to the exhaustive (column) reduction: the fully reduced matrix is unique.

svg.text: j ← lft(i) ▷ earliest column with low(j) = i
for j′ > j with R[i, j′] ≠ 0: ▷ every column to the right
▷ row i becomes zero right of its pivot: this yields
